meters.label: Attack URLs that reached the inside (of 7)

frames.narration: A photo app imports a picture from a URL the user pastes. The server fetches it. The server can reach internal services that the internet cannot.
With no check, the attacker pastes an internal address. The server fetches it from the inside and returns the answer. Six of the seven attack URLs work.

A deny-list of strings blocks localhost and the metadata address as typed. The attacker writes loopback as one decimal number, or uses a hostname that resolves to a private address. Four still get through.
Checking the resolved address closes the spellings and the names. But the fetcher resolves the name once to check and again to connect, and redirects are followed without a check. Three get through.
An allow-list of hosts stops almost everything: only your CDN and image host are fetched. One hole remains, an open redirect on an allowed host. And a real partner is now refused.
The last variant resolves once, refuses private addresses, connects to that same address and does not follow redirects. Zero attack URLs reach the inside.
Maintenance is the price: add the partner's domain to the allow-list after review and all 3 legitimate URLs work again.
Defence in depth around the code: egress rules that let the fetcher reach only the internet, a token required by the metadata service, and no raw responses returned to the user.

states.internal: needs a token, blocked by egress rules
